title: One CPV dip requires thick dust for opacity index 1 but permits a thin screen for index 0.25
abstract: We derive bounds on dust columns from two simultaneous dip depths, while allowing any distribution of optical depth across the star. We apply the bounds to the deepest TESS and 2.09 micrometer dip of TIC 300651846 in published photometry from 2025 February 11. For an intrinsic opacity proportional to wavelength to the power -1, at least 48.0% of the infrared dip comes from columns with infrared optical depth at least one. A conservative joint 95% lower bound is 20.7%. The brightness coverage of these columns is at least 1.57%, with a joint lower bound of 0.63%. A finite uniform screen with opacity index 0.25 fits the same central depths with infrared optical depth 0.188 and coverage 19.1%. Thus the inference of thick dust depends on the intrinsic opacity law. We prove that finite colors with nonzero errors cannot establish an infinite optical depth or the spatial shape of a core. This use of partial coverage gives analytic bounds and explicit alternatives, not a new dust detection. Common surface color, a shared screen, Gaussian marginal errors and effective wavelengths limit the application. The package includes proofs, code, numerical checks, source hashes and separate-scratch retrieval instructions.

display.caption: Conditional bounds for the main dip of TIC 300651846, and finite uniform screens that fit both central depths. Source measurements: Bouma et al. (2026), Table 4. Predictions outside the measured bands are examples, not allowed envelopes.
